text:
Alex Kim: quick heads-up — after PTQ (q4) on the new 7B reranker we’re seeing a noticeable quality dip: NDCG@10 -2.7% absolute, MRR@10 -1.9% on dev. creating thread to triage slices and formatting effects.
Maria G: which eval set? ms-marco or internal logs? also paste the eval command you ran.
Alex Kim: ran on internal-relevance-v3 (mix of web+support queries). command: 
```
python eval.py --model checkpoints/7b_ptq_q4 --data data/internal-relevance-v3.jsonl --qformat raw --docformat trunc-384 --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10 --seed 42
```
results (dev summary):
```
ndcg@10: 0.642 -> 0.615  (-0.027)
mrr@10: 0.514 -> 0.495  (-0.019)
```
Samir Patel: thanks. do we have per-slice breakdown? small queries vs long queries, exact-match heavy queries, brand queries?
Alex Kim: attached quick slice CSV (snippet):
```
slice,base_ndcg,new_ndcg,delta
short_query,len<=10,0.672,0.669,-0.003
long_query,doc_len>1024,0.591,0.548,-0.043
brand_query,contains_brand,0.701,0.695,-0.006
typo_queries,lev<=2,0.610,0.588,-0.022
```
Chris O'Neill: big red flag: long-doc slice has biggest drop. could be quantization sensitivity with attention patterns when truncation interacts with KV-cache. Also check doc formatting: trunc-384 might cut different tokens depending on tokenizer.
Maria G: good call. try two quick ablations: (A) eval with `docformat full-2048` (no truncation) (B) eval with `tokenizer=parity` using the same tokenization as train (we suspect vocab/clipping differences). also try `--normalize-queries` (lowercase+strip-punct).
Samir Patel: also run paired bootstrap CI for ndcg deltas. code: 
```
python bootstrap_diff.py --preds base_preds.npy new_preds.npy --metric ndcg@10 --iters 5000 --out ci.json
```
EvalBot: bootstrap result uploaded: `{"ndcg_delta": -0.027, "p_value": 0.028, "95ci": [-0.039, -0.014]}`
Maria G: p=0.028 so likely not noise. next we should isolate tokenizer vs quantization. can someone run `ptq=false` on the exact same checkpoint and compare?
Alex Kim: ran quick check — disabled PTQ (fp16) -> NDCG@10 recovered to -0.004 from baseline (almost parity). so root cause seems PTQ sensitivity.
Chris O'Neill: interesting. PTQ sensitive for long docs makes sense. two suspects: (1) small rounding errors accumulate in attention scores on long sequences, (2) quantized KV-cache indexing mismatch for our tokenizer truncation.
Samir Patel: try targeted smaller quant params: per-channel vs per-tensor, and calibration set size. also run quantization with `--calib-set long-docs-only` to see if calibration bias helps.
Maria G: action items:
- Maria G: run tokenization parity and `--normalize-queries` ablation (by EOD)
- Chris O'Neill: run doc-length bucketing + full-2048 run to confirm KV/trunc interaction (tomorrow)
- Samir Patel: run PTQ variants (per-channel, calib-size) + bootstrap tests (48h)
- Alex Kim: collect sample failure cases (10 each) and add paraphrase augmentation experiment (smaller set).
Alex Kim: quick note on query formatting: when we tried `--normalize-queries` (lowercase + strip punctuation) on a small subset, short queries didn't change much but tail typo queries improved ~0.01 ndcg, long-docs unchanged. paraphrase augmentation gave +0.006 on tail but didn't fix long-doc drop.
Chris O'Neill: if PTQ remains the limiter, consider shipping fallback policy: route long-doc queries to fp16 model or lower-quantization variant until we fix. Redwood routing can do that via model-variant policy.
Maria G: agree. also we should add a slice-based regression alert in the console: ndcg drop >0.02 for doc_len>1024.
Samir Patel: leaving notes for reproducer: ensure same seeds, same tokenizers, and export topk preds for paired test. small script to collect topk: 
```
python collect_topk.py --preds checkpoints/* --qfile q.jsonl --k 10 --out topk_dir/
```
EvalBot: CI note: I queued `ptq=per-channel` job and will post summary when done.
Alex Kim: thanks all — will post the failure samples and a short doc with the ablation matrix once we have the PTQ variant results. :thumbsup:
